articles.full_text:
File image
The India Meteorological Department has issued a 'yellow' alert for Nanded district for October 17 and 18, warning of thunderstorms, lightning and light to moderate rain in isolated places.
The IMD's Regional Meteorological Centre in Mumbai said gusty winds with speeds of 30-40 kmph are likely during this period.
District officials said all departments have been asked to remain alert and take necessary precautionary measures, while residents have been urged to exercise caution.
People are advised against venturing outdoors during lightning, an official said on Thursday.
"They should switch off electrical appliances and stay away from electric poles, wire fences and other metal objects. Anyone standing in water should immediately move to a dry place. People should refrain from using landline telephones, taking showers, touching taps or water pipes, and operating electrical appliances during lightning," he said.

articles.full_text:
Rain-slicked streets reflect the dazzling neonlight displays set up at Poojapura as part of the Navratri celebrations in Thiruvananthapuram on Thursday.
| Photo Credit: NIRMAL HARINDRAN
Northeast monsoon set in over Keralam on Thursday, with easterly and northeasterly winds establishing over southern peninsular India, the specialty of the northeast monsoon.
A weather bulletin issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Thursday confirmed the withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from the country and the simultaneous beginning of the northeast monsoon rainfall activity over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka, Kerala, and Mahe.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over south coastal Tamil Nadu and the neighbourhood in lower tropospheric levels, along with supporting systems in the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea. Fairly widespread rainfall is expected over Keralam on Friday. The opening day was marked by a cloudy sky with a few spells of thundershowers along the ghat regions in the State.
A yellow alert has been issued for the entire State on Friday, where isolated thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds with speeds reaching 40-50 kmph is expected on the day. Ahead of the arrival of the northeast monsoon, maximum temperature fell appreciably in Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram districts, and there was no large change in it elsewhere over Keralam during the past 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Thursday.
However, it was above normal in parts of north and central Keralam, especially in Kozhikode and Palakkad districts. According to the weather bulletin, maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 32°C and 25°C, respectively, in the coming days.
